CLAS 220.description: Major gods, goddesses, heroes, and heroines of classical mythology as portrayed in major literary works; the function of myth in society and its relevance to modern life.
CLAS 220.subject: CLAS
CLAS 220.title: Introduction to Classical Mythology

CLAS 230.description: Greek and Latin elements in the formation of medical and scientific vocabulary; designed for students intending to enter the scientific and health professions. No previous knowledge of Greek or Latin required.
CLAS 230.subject: CLAS
CLAS 230.title: Medical and Scientific Terminology

CLAS 240.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the importance of competition in the military and private spheres of the Greco-Roman world, a dominant legacy of antiquity.
CLAS 240.subject: CLAS
CLAS 240.title: Sport and Combat in the Ancient World

CLAS 301.description: An introduction to the work of ancient philosophers, with special emphasis on Plato and Aristotle.
CLAS 301.subject: CLAS
CLAS 301.title: Ancient Philosophy

CLAS 302.description: Problems such as hedonism, providence, belief and evidence, and mysticism, as they appear in the writings of Epicureans, Stoics, Skeptics, and Plotinus.
CLAS 302.subject: CLAS
CLAS 302.title: Greek and Roman Philosophy after Aristotle

CLAS 305.description: Representations of antiquity in cinema, television, and other contemporary media, with emphasis on Hollywood’s reception of Greek and Roman history.
CLAS 305.subject: CLAS
CLAS 305.title: Greece and Rome in Film and Popular Culture

CLAS 320.description: Gender roles, standards of sexual behavior, evidence for women’s lives, as manifested in ancient Greek literary and archaeological evidence; attitudes toward homosexuality; the modern media’s representation of famous Greeks.
CLAS 320.subject: CLAS
CLAS 320.title: Sexuality and Gender in Ancient Greece

CLAS 321.description: Sexuality as a social construct exemplified in standards of sexual behavior in ancient Rome and their reinforcement of the ruling ideology; feminine virtue, definitions of manliness, attitudes toward homosexuality.
CLAS 321.subject: CLAS
CLAS 321.title: Sexuality, Gender, and Power in Ancient Rome

CLAS 323.description: Introduction to the history and culture of ancient Greece, combined with an excursion of Greece. Topics include: Mycenaean Greece and the world of Homer, Archaic Greece, oikos and polis, interaction with the Near East, Athens in the 5th and 4th centruy BCE, Greek religion, ancient Greek society.
CLAS 323.subject: CLAS
CLAS 323.title: Greek Civilization on Site

CLAS 324.description: Intensive study of one topic per semester dealing with ancient contributions to Western civilization. Not for Greek or Latin major credit. In English. May be repeated as content varies by title.
CLAS 324.subject: CLAS
CLAS 324.title: Special Topics in Classical Humanities

CLAS 325.description: Study of the impact of the culture of Greece and Rome on the founding fathers of the American Revolution.
CLAS 325.subject: CLAS
CLAS 325.title: Classical Roots of US Constitution

CLAS 333.description: Introduction to the history and culture of ancient Rome through direct participation in archaeological excavations at select ancient Roman sites in a hands-on learning environment.
CLAS 333.subject: CLAS
CLAS 333.title: Roman Civilization On Site

CLAS 340.description: A survey of ancient architecture, painting, and sculpture 2000-160 B.C.
CLAS 340.subject: CLAS
CLAS 340.title: Greek Art and Archaeology

CLAS 350.description: This course uses the rich archaeological resource of the city of Pompeii to explore daily life in Ancient Rome. Using both material and written sources, students will learn about how people of all social classes lived in the public and private spaces of Pompeii.
CLAS 350.subject: CLAS
CLAS 350.title: Pompeii: Daily Life in a Roman Town

CLAS 360.description: Examination of ancient Greek and Roman philosophical, medical, and literary works (in English) as sources for the origins of medical ethics. Priority enrollment for Medical Humanities students.
CLAS 360.subject: CLAS
CLAS 360.title: Classical Origins of Western Medical Ethics

CLAS 361.description: Introduction to ancient medicine: science and art, theory and practice, healing and predicting. Topics include Medicine before Hippocrates, Hippocratic medicine, holism, naturalism, medicine, religion and magic, medicine and scientific explanation, Hellenistic medicine and methodology, Galenic medicine.
CLAS 361.subject: CLAS
CLAS 361.title: Between Magic and Method: Ancient Medicine

CLAS 370.description: Athenian History from Persian Wars through Peloponnesian War.
CLAS 370.subject: CLAS
CLAS 370.title: Rise and Fall of the Athenian Empire

CLAS 371.description: Study of Rome’s imperial family from Julius Caesar until the death of Nero.
CLAS 371.subject: CLAS
CLAS 371.title: The Caesars: Rome's First Family

CLAS 372.description: In-depth study of the history, literature and culture of the Greek world era of Alexander the Great.
CLAS 372.subject: CLAS
CLAS 372.title: The Age of Alexander the Great

CLAS 373.description: Historical, literary, and cultural study of the Roman Empire during its final years of dominance in the West.
CLAS 373.subject: CLAS
CLAS 373.title: The Fall of the Roman Empire

CLAS 380.description: Study of the development of the novel as a literary genre in ancient Greece and Rome.
CLAS 380.subject: CLAS
CLAS 380.title: The Ancient Novel

CLAS 381.description: A study of Plutarch’s biographies of some of the most important historical figures from ancient Greece and Rome.
CLAS 381.subject: CLAS
CLAS 381.title: Plutarch's Lives of Greeks and Romans

CLAS 401.description: A comparative survey of Greek and Latin masters.
CLAS 401.subject: CLAS
CLAS 401.title: Greek and Latin Literature in Translation

CLAS 469.description: Representative plays by Greek and Roman dramatists.
CLAS 469.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ENGL 101 and ENGL 102.
CLAS 469.subject: CLAS
CLAS 469.title: Classical Drama

CLAS 471.description: Classical rhetoric and its ongoing influence in the modern world, emphasizing how the study and use of language in ancient Greece and Rome continue to shape modern communication.
CLAS 471.subject: CLAS
CLAS 471.title: Rhetoric and the Ancient Roots of Modern Life

CLAS 586.description: The major Greek and Roman myths, with emphasis on their meaning, functions, and influence on ancient and later Western culture.
CLAS 586.subject: CLAS
CLAS 586.title: Classical Mythology

CLAS 598.description: Problems of literary theory in texts from the ancients to the 17th century, with an emphasis on the classical tradition.
CLAS 598.subject: CLAS
CLAS 598.title: Classics of Western Literary Theory

CLAS 777.description: Supervised direction of foreign language teaching in college. Required of all graduate assistants who are teaching. This course will not count toward the MA or PhD degree.
CLAS 777.subject: CLAS
CLAS 777.title: Supervised Instruction in Teaching Foreign Languages in College
